elements.element: Customer has no MFN-related obligation to disclose third-party offers or terms to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Original § 7.2, which required Customer to disclose more favourable offers, is omitted from the rendered clause. Section 12.3 also states that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

elements.element: Customer has no MFN-related obligation to match or extend more favourable third-party offers or terms to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The matching obligation in original § 7.2 has been deleted, and § 12.3 affirmatively disclaims any most-favoured-customer commitment by Customer.

elements.element: Customer has no other MFN or most-favoured-customer obligation benefiting Vendor or otherwise burdening Customer.
elements.evidence: The remaining operative language states that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. It does not prohibit a separate MFN right benefiting Customer.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer applies only to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: This requirement is conditional on an MFN obligation burdening Customer. That condition is demonstrably absent because § 7.2 was deleted and § 12.3 states that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No Customer-burdening MFN obligation remains, so there is no obligation capable of exceeding the 12-month fallback limit.

elements.element: Any 12-month MFN period begins from a specified commencement trigger.
elements.evidence: The triggering condition is absent: the operative language imposes no MFN obligation on Customer.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer excludes offers or transactions that are not reasonably comparable because of material commercial differences.
elements.evidence: No Customer-burdening MFN obligation remains. Accordingly, no non-comparable offer can trigger a disclosure, matching, or parity duty.

result.reason: The operative redline deletes the only disclosure-and-matching MFN obligation and retains the express acknowledgment that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. This fully achieves the preferred position; the fallback limitations are also satisfied because their predicate—an MFN burdening Customer—is demonstrably absent. The deletion is targeted, resolves the inconsistency between former § 7.2 and § 12.3, and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
